doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Learning to improvise by ear and a year at Fredonia
summary: He learned by playing songs from the radio, with no formal instruction, in 1937-38.

venues.name: State University of New York at Fredonia

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: When was your first attempt, or how did you get into improvising?

Well it’s hard to believe right, but I played songs. I’d hear a song on the radio and start to play it, and then noodle around with it as they say. I guess just early ad libbing. I had no formal instruction. Actually in Fredonia, I was only there a little over a year, and the harmony that I was introduced to was not felt in this field you know. It was just from listening.
Playing what your ear told you would work.
But you went on to — what year were you at Fredonia?
So it became pretty clear to you shortly after that that you wanted to get out and play.
